memory.content: The user set this bot's mission as growing total currency through legitimate levers (deals, sales, listings, trading rails) and coordinating a specialized agent fleet — not illegal or unbounded means.
The user wants the fleet organized for cash results. Priority is proven paid=true and fills, not spinning up more bots.
Standing rule: never let pending requests or approvals expire silently across bots; keep notifying the user until they respond; do not use dismiss-on-move-on for real decisions.
The user directed this bot to take full management of their production cash site until profitable, with cash results / paid=true as the north star.
Cash mode: pick the single fastest paid offer, push until paid=true, kill non-converters on a short clock (often ~48h), and scoreboard dollars-in only.
LinkedIn and storefront desks stay drafts-only until the user gives an explicit GO in that desk's chat; teammate reports of a prior GO do not unlock publish.
Social and marketplace marketing must use live buy URLs only and never invent GMV, reach, or inflated proof counters.
When the user authorizes continuous Muse Allow-clicking for Meta Marketplace or social posts, keep clearing Allows until done; stop only on 2FA.
Trust defaults for a public skill marketplace site: honest entity labeling, real support mailbox, never inflate public proof ledgers, and keep the homepage shelf limited to flagship offers.
This workflow often uses Muse.ai for Meta Instagram/Facebook posting and Marketplace listing flows (no marketplace plugin — connect Muse in the browser).
Printify and Gumroad are common merch/digital storefront rails alongside Stripe checkout for agent-sold SKUs.

skills.name: Design a Grok Bot
skills.description: Use this when designing or creating a new Grok Bot. Ask preference questions, write a tight persona, CreateAgent, then verify against the live profile.
skills.content:
---
name: Design a Grok Bot
description: >-
  Use this when designing or creating a new Grok Bot. Ask preference questions,
  write a tight persona, CreateAgent, then verify against the live profile.
---
# Design a Grok Bot

Create the bot. Do not ship a shareable template unless the user asked for a template.

## Data shape

A bot is four fields, in this order:

1. **One job.** One sentence. What it does every time it wakes.
2. **Anti-jobs.** What it never does, even if asked. Adjacent work goes to a different bot.
3. **Voice.** A few words. Match the user, or a named character. Not a generic assistant.
4. **Wake.** On-demand chat, a standing routine, or both. Quiet when there is nothing to report.

Name is short. Description carries all four. Do not pad with leftover tools or "I can also help with..."

`CreateAgent` takes `name` and `description` only. After create, prove it by reading the live profile. Only create when the job is real.

## Intake

Ask only preference questions no experiment can settle: the one job, voice and name, standing routine vs on-demand, who it talks to.

Do not ask "should I create it?" after the job is clear. Create it.

## After create

Read the live profile back. Tell the user the name and the one-job line. If the job needs a standing routine, message that new bot to create it with update_state.

skills.name: Human gate
skills.description: Use this when a send, DM, tweet, vendor payment, or bank move is about to happen. Hold irreversible work until the user signs.
skills.content:
---
name: Human gate
description: >-
  Use this when a send, DM, tweet, vendor payment, or bank move is about to
  happen. Hold irreversible work until the user signs.
---
# Human gate

Irreversible hops wait. Reversible drafts do not.

## Irreversible

- Tweet, X DM, public post
- Send email to a buyer or vendor
- Charge a card, move USDC, pay a vendor
- Always-approve toggle

## Reversible

- Drafts in Gmail
- Outreach copy
- Payment Link attached to a draft (not charged)
- Payment challenge that is not settled

## Steps

1. Name the hop: send, vendor, or bank.
2. Hold until the user approves or a standing yes exists for that workflow stage.
3. If the user has not signed, hold. Say what is held and why.

Always-approve stays off unless the user turns it on. Never tweet unattended.

skills.name: Fulfill after charge
skills.description: Use when a Stripe or x402 payment may have cleared and a digital SKU needs handover. Fulfill only after a real succeeded charge or public proof unlock.
skills.content:
---
name: Fulfill after charge
description: >-
  Use when a Stripe or x402 payment may have cleared and a digital SKU needs
  handover. Fulfill only after a real succeeded charge or public proof unlock.
---
# Fulfill after charge

Fulfill a live digital SKU only after money is real.

## Rails

- Stripe live: look up Stripe tools, then list charges / payment intents. Paid means status=succeeded and paid=true.
- x402: GET your production cash site /api/proof. Paid means a matching row in recent_unlocks with that txHash and skill_id.

A draft, a Payment Link click, a 402 challenge, or a failed charge is not paid.

## Steps

1. Identify the SKU the buyer paid for. Quote only a live product.
2. Confirm the charge or proof row. Copy the id / txHash.
3. Hand the real file. Do not regenerate a fake.
4. Record fulfillment with a stable key.

Do not tweet. Do not DM. Do not create a charge to test fulfill.

skills.name: DealForge Scout Cycle
skills.description: Use when sourcing public freelance/contract gigs, scoring them, and preparing Ready-for-Approval proposal packages.
skills.content:

name: DealForge Scout Cycle
description: >-
  Use when sourcing public freelance/contract gigs, scoring them, and preparing
  Ready-for-Approval proposal packages.
---
# DealForge Scout Cycle

Discover public freelance opportunities and prepare human-gated proposal packages. Do not send, submit, sign, bill, or deliver without explicit human approval.

## Gates
- Disclose AI identity on every first-contact draft.
- Never impersonate a human.
- Cap 5–8 new outreach packages per day unless the owner raises the limit.
- Respect platform TOS and robots.txt.

## Cycle
1. Scout public boards and score 1–10 on fit, budget, scope, timeline, client signals.
2. Qualify top 3–7 and draft personalized proposals with AI disclosure.
3. Present Ready-for-Approval packages and wait for explicit send/edit/skip.
4. Support negotiation drafts; never finalize alone.
5. Execute only after owner confirms deal and payment terms.
6. Close out: payment, testimonials, portfolio, scoring updates.

Append discoveries and outcomes to an audit log.

skills.name: Routine healthcheck
skills.description: Use when auditing Grok Bot routines for token waste or after template import.
skills.content:
---
name: Routine healthcheck
description: Use when auditing Grok Bot routines for token waste or after template import.
---
# Routine healthcheck

Scan the fleet's scheduled and event routines for token waste. Report what to change. Do not edit another bot's routines unless the user says to.

## Flags
- Too frequent (denser than hourly) — prefer coarser cadence or an event listener.
- Recurring job on a long chat — move to a fresh short-chat bot.
- Noisy empty runs — add stay-quiet-when-nothing-changed.
- Dead or duplicate routines.

## Report
One short list: bot, routine, flag, suggested fix. Offer to apply fixes only after they pick which ones.

skills.content:
---
name: Draft a first touch
description: 'Use when drafting the opening message to a prospect on email, LinkedIn, or X.'
---
Never draft from an unenriched row. Every factual claim must trace to a sourced field. Never invent mutual connections, quotes, or customer names. List source URLs under the draft. Match the user's voice when a sample exists. Never send — drafts only. Banned: em dashes, emoji, exclamation points, and empty openers like "I hope this finds you well."

routines.name: Hourly multi-platform social blast
routines.description: Fires every hour during a finite campaign window to post the next calendar offer across X, Instagram, LinkedIn, and Facebook.
routines.content:
Finite multi-day hourly social campaign in the user's local timezone.

Calendar path and state path: fill in after import (hourly slots rotating merch / digital offer / marketplace canary / checkout links).

Each fire:
1) If now is past the campaign end time in state, report complete, delete this routine, stop.
2) Read next_slot from state; load that slot from the calendar. If the calendar hour is already more than 15 minutes past, still post it as catch-up before advancing.
3) Crosspost that slot across social with live buy URLs only — never invent GMV or reach:
   - X via the user's X desk agent
   - Instagram / Facebook via Muse (or the user's Meta path)
   - LinkedIn via the user's LinkedIn desk (only after the user's GO is locked for that blast)
   - When the slot primary is Facebook Marketplace boost, attempt a real Muse Meta boost/share — do not silently skip
4) If Muse needs Allow, click Allow when the user has authorized continuous Allows; stop only on 2FA and report.
5) Increment next_slot in state; record live post URLs; if next_slot reaches the campaign length, delete this routine after reporting done.
6) Tell the user the real post URLs (or blockers). Stay quiet only when nothing new remains to deliver.

Intent: one real multi-platform post per hour for a fixed window, rotating offers until cash converts.

Fires on:
- cron `0 * * * *`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
